title_prefix: getdeploymentinfo never emits the bip9 s
mechanism: Confirmed as written. Core threads a per-block signalling vector through the whole statistics path: GetStateStatisticsFor takes an out-parameter std::vector<bool>* signalling_blocks, sizes it to blocks_in_period = 1 + (nHeight % period) and sets one entry per block of the current period as it walks backwards testing Condition (versionbits.cpp:118-155); VersionBitsCache::Info fills BIP9Info::signalling_blocks whenever the current state is STARTED or LOCKED_IN (versionbits.cpp:207-217, versionbits.h:58-59); and SoftForkDescPushBack turns it into a string of '#' for a signalling block and '-' for a non-signalling one, pushed as "signalling" immediately after the statistics object and inside the same has_value guard (rpc/blockchain.cpp:1332-1349). Ours has no such thing anywhere. bl.val:versionbits-statistics (src/validation/versionbits.lisp:308-338) returns only (period threshold elapsed count possible) -- it walks the same blocks and calls the same %vb-condition-p, but discards which ones matched -- and %bip9-deployment (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:2494-2544) builds bit, start_time, timeout, min_activation_height, status, since, status_next and statistics and stops. A live sweep of every fbound symbol in BITCOIN-LISP.VALIDATION and BITCOIN-LISP.RPC whose name contains SIGNALL returned NIL, and a grep of src/ for "signalling" finds no producer, so the absence is total rather than a naming difference.
consequence: Kept at S3. Nothing acts on this string: it is a per-block view of who signalled in the current period, which an operator watching an activation reads and a client displays. Two concrete effects. First, Core's rpc_blockchain.py asserts it inside an assert_equal of the WHOLE getdeploymentinfo result (check_signalling_deploymentinfo_result, rpc_blockchain.py:210-258, with 'signalling': '#'*(height-143) at :240), called three times -- at height 207, at height 287, and again by blockhash at :283 -- so all three fail on the missing key alone even though every other field in that object matches. Executed here, the testdummy bip9 object at height 207 of a 300-block chain signalling bit 28 came back field for field as Core's expected dict (bit 28, start_time 0, timeout 9223372036854775807, min_activation_height 0, status "started", since 144, status_next "started", statistics period 144 / elapsed 64 / count 64 / threshold 108 / possible true) with "signalling" simply absent. Second, an operator loses the only per-block view the RPC offers: count and elapsed say 64 of 64, but not which 64, so a period where signalling stopped part-way looks the same as one where it was continuous until the aggregate counters diverge. That is a reporting gap, not a wrong value, and the aggregate numbers it sits next to are correct, so it stays at S3.
evidence: Probe build/ga11v/p-vb.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-rpcutil-s3a, warm image bitcoin-lisp-dev-e618132ea0cf). make-versionbits-chain 300 :signal-bit 28, then bl.rpc::%bip9-deployments at the ancestor entries for heights 207, 287, 288 and 299 with bl:*network* :regtest (regtest testdummy: bit 28, start 0, no timeout, threshold 108, period 144 -- src/validation/versionbits.lisp:77-81, transcribed from kernel/chainparams.cpp:580-591). Height 207 => (("testdummy" ("active" . FALSE) ("type" . "bip9") ("bip9" ("bit" . 28) ("start_time" . 0) ("timeout" . 9223372036854775807) ("min_activation_height" . 0) ("status" . "started") ("since" . 144) ("status_next" . "started") ("statistics" ("period" . 144) ("elapsed" . 64) ("count" . 64) ("threshold" . 108) ("possible" . T)))) ("taproot" ...)) -- no "signalling" key. Height 299 (status locked_in, since 288) likewise has statistics and no "signalling", so the omission covers both states in which Core emits it. elapsed 64 at height 207 equals Core's expected height-143 = 64 and count equals elapsed, so the underlying walk is right and only the per-block record is thrown away. Absence sweep: (do-symbols over BITCOIN-LISP.VALIDATION and BITCOIN-LISP.RPC collecting fbound symbols whose name contains "SIGNALL") => NIL. Files: src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:2494-2544; src/validation/versionbits.lisp:308-338; refs/bitcoin/src/versionbits.cpp:118-155,207-217; refs/bitcoin/src/versionbits.h:49-62; refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp:1332-1349; refs/bitcoin/test/functional/rpc_blockchain.py:210-258,275-283.
fix_shape: Carry the per-block record out of the walk that already computes it, rather than recomputing it in the RPC. Give bl.val:versionbits-statistics a sixth return value: a bit vector (or a simple-bit-vector of length elapsed) whose element i is 1 when the block at offset i from the start of the current period satisfied %vb-condition-p. Core indexes it from the START of the period -- it assigns blocks_in_period entries and writes at the decreasing index as it walks backwards from the tip (versionbits.cpp:130-147) -- so the first character of the string is the period's first block and the last is the block being reported on; getting that order backwards is the easy mistake and is exactly what the '#'*(height-143) assertion cannot catch on an all-signalling chain, so the test for it must use a chain where only some blocks signal. Then in %bip9-deployment, inside the existing `counting` branch and immediately after the statistics pair, push ("signalling" . <string>) built by mapping 1 to #\# and 0 to #\-. Nothing else moves: the guard is already Core's (current state STARTED or LOCKED_IN), and the string is empty-safe because elapsed is at least 1 whenever an entry exists. Test with a chain whose bit-28 blocks are interleaved -- assert the exact string, not its length -- and keep an all-signalling chain as the control that reproduces Core's '#'*(height-143) at heights 207 and 287.
